Opacity

A 0–100 scale in 5% steps, three named aliases for disabled and hover states, and pre-mixed white and black for tints over artwork. Fade a whole element with the scale; tint a colour with a ramp or color-mix().

21 steps3 aliases2 rampsToken-driven

Scale

Each swatch is --color-primary at opacity: var(--opacity-*), over a checkerboard. Tokens are --opacity-0 to --opacity-100.

Transparency ramps

White and black pre-mixed as 8-digit hex, for a tint that has to sit over unknown artwork — the on-dark surfaces use them. White is shown over a dark checkerboard, black over a light one. For a tint of a semantic colour use color-mix() over the token instead, so it follows into dark mode.
AlphaWhiteBlackHex
1%--transparent-white-1--transparent-black-1#FFFFFF03 · #00000003
5%--transparent-white-5--transparent-black-5#FFFFFF0D · #0000000D
10%--transparent-white-10--transparent-black-10#FFFFFF1A · #0000001A
20%--transparent-white-20--transparent-black-20#FFFFFF33 · #00000033
30%--transparent-white-30--transparent-black-30#FFFFFF4D · #0000004D
40%--transparent-white-40--transparent-black-40#FFFFFF66 · #00000066
50%--transparent-white-50--transparent-black-50#FFFFFF80 · #00000080

Guidelines

✓ Do
  • Use an alias for a state, so the state moves as one.
  • Tint a colour with color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 10%, transparent) — the text on it stays solid.
  • Pair a dimmed control with disabled or aria-disabled; opacity alone says nothing to a screen reader.
✗ Don't
  • Don’t fade a whole element to make a tint — its text and border fade with it.
  • Don’t nest faded elements; opacities multiply (50% inside 50% is 25%).
  • Don’t use a white or black ramp for a semantic colour; it will not follow into dark mode.
